sentences.text: An inboard boat steers by water flowing past the rudder, mostly prop wash.
At low speed, especially in reverse, there’s little flow, and steering is poor.
A short burst of power with the rudder over gives steering without building much speed.
Going ahead, a boat pivots about a point roughly a third of its length back from the bow, so the stern swings wide in a turn, which matters when you’re turning near a dock or another boat.
Outboards and sterndrives steer by aiming the propeller’s thrust, so they respond well even at low speed.
